title: Hosted API — Hourly burst margin simulation (by region)
summary: Spreadsheet-backed sensitivity simulation that models short (1–6h) hourly burst events by region and estimates effective per-token COGS, PPK, and margin at current list prices. Intention: inform reserve+spot mix, routing rules, and short-term surge playbook.
content:
Background:
- We see repeatable short-duration load spikes across customers (daily peaks, batch jobs, marketing-driven bursts). These bursts matter because they force upward SKU/slot tiling and reduce amortization efficiencies, driving up marginal per-token COGS for the hour(s) of the event.

Goal:
- Build a lightweight scenario matrix that:
  * Simulates 1h, 3h, and 6h burst shapes at 2x/3x/5x of baseline request rate
  * Applies region-specific cost profiles (US, EU, APAC) reflecting GPU-hour, power, and license amortization
  * Models cache hit-rate sensitivity (0%, 20%, 50%) and model blend fallbacks (full -> quantized -> smaller model)
  * Outputs effective PPK (per-1k-token cost), incremental COGS during burst, and margin at current hosted API price points

Assumptions (simplified for spreadsheet):
- Baseline request shape: avg tokens per request = 120; baseline throughput per slot = 200k tokens/hour for default model (float32) under current runtime tuning.
- Pricing (example list): retail price = $0.0012 per token (hosted list, illustrative).
- Region GPU amortization per GPU-hour: US = $2.40, EU = $2.70, APAC = $3.10 (includes infra, power, license amortization mapped to a token-level basis depending on utilization).
- Spot availability reduces GPU-hour amort by 40% when available; reserved reduces by 20% (mix is tunable).
- Cache: prefix/KV caching reduces generation tokens by ratio of hit-rate * avg-prefix-length (we approximate as tokens saved per request).
- Model blend: fallback to quantized variant reduces per-token runtime cost by ~30% but increases quality risk; fallback to a smaller model reduces cost by ~60% but may not be compatible with all prompts.

Methodology overview (spreadsheet tabs):
- assumptions: raw input params above (editable)
- region-costs: per-GPU-hour, network egress, avg-power, regional multipliers
- burst-scenarios: definition table of shapes (1h/3h/6h * 2x/3x/5x)
- utilization-sim: translates request rate into required slot counts under continuous batching assumptions
- ppk-calcs: per-scenario PPK, incremental cost, margin at pricing

Sample scenario snapshots (CSV rows included in "tables" field below). The spreadsheet runs across three region sheets and aggregates into a dashboard: incremental-ppk, margin-impact, recommended-routing-action.

Key outputs (high level, from simulated sheet):
- Example: US region, 1h 3x burst, cache hit 20%, spot mix 30%:
  * Effective COGS per 1k tokens (PPK): $0.42
  * Incremental hourly COGS vs baseline: +72%
  * Margin at $0.0012/token (i.e., $1.20 per 1k tokens): 65%
- Example: APAC region, 6h 5x burst, cache 0%, spot unavailable:
  * Effective PPK: $0.92
  * Incremental hourly COGS: +210%
  * Margin: 23%

Topline recommendations from simulation run:
1) Short-term routing: for predictable short bursts (marketing windows, batch imports) prefer region routing to US/EU where PPK headroom is higher; automatically prefer quantized fallback if quality guardrails pass.
2) Reserve/spot mix policy: preserve >=30% spot pool for baseline and short bursts; for multi-hour sustained surges (>=3h) shift a portion of traffic to reserved to avoid repeated preemption churn costs.
3) Cache posture: deploy aggressive prefix caching for templates-heavy customers (we estimate up to 35–50% token savings for prompt-heavy workflows). Prioritize cache pre-warm for scheduled marketing windows.
4) Surge SKUs and pricing: expose an optional surge premium SKU to customers who need guaranteed latency during bursts (blended price that retains ~40–50% margin).
5) Observability hooks: add hourly PPK telemetry and a short-burst anomaly detector to tag customers with a burst index for targeted cost recovery/credits.

Operational playbook snippets (to translate sheet into ops):
- If the hourly burst increases required slots by >2x and spot-preempt rate >15% -> trigger auto-fallback to quantized model and enable regional spillover.
- If predicted burst >4x and duration >3h -> proactively allocate reserved pool (one-time quick reserve carve out) for top 5 customers causing load.
- For scheduled bursts: require pre-notification window of 24–72h to allow prefill of cache and reserve capacity.

Open questions and knobs for follow-up (TODOs):
- Validate real GPU-hour amortization numbers across clouds and instance families (we used blended estimates). Need infra finance breakdown per instance type.
- Measure actual tokens saved by KV/prefix cache for top 20 customers to firm up cache-hit assumptions.
- Model quality impact of quantized fallback across our eval prompt set (regression risk).
- Add slot startup/shutdown cost (cold-start impact) into the 1h burst model — currently we assume instant elasticity.

Notes to self / quick checks: 
- Link to current reserve inventory sheet (linked_artifacts) for verifying spot/reserve mix assumptions.
- Cross-check retail price used vs pricing-engine live table before shipping recommendations.

Appendix: small excerpt of the scenario table exported from sheet (comma-separated rows) is in the "tables" field. This is what the dashboard tab consumes for the charts and thresholds.

Formatting: This Drive doc is a companion to the sheet itself — use it to capture rationale and decisions. The sheet will be the source of truth for numeric toggles.

Unresolved: Where to account for downstream costs (embeddings, retrieval) that may multiply token counts in some customers' workloads — currently out of scope for this spike model.
